channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Machine Learning versus Deep Learning: A Distinction That Matters
item.description: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning, not a replacement for it. Confusing the two leads to wasted compute and weaker baselines.

item.title: Comparing Two ML Models Without Fooling Yourself
item.description: A higher accuracy score does not mean a better model. Here is a practical, honest way to test whether the difference between two models is real.

item.title: Vector Databases and RAG, Explained Simply
item.description: How embeddings and vector search let language models look things up instead of guessing, and why the plumbing matters more than the hype.

item.title: Prompt Engineering versus Fine-Tuning: Choosing the Lever
item.description: A practical guide to choosing between prompt engineering and fine-tuning, with a worked example showing when each lever actually pays off.

item.title: Named Entity Recognition: Three Approaches Compared
item.description: A practical comparison of rule-based, statistical, and neural NER, with a worked example showing where each approach wins and where it quietly fails.

item.title: Monitoring Model Drift: What to Log and When to Retrain
item.description: Drift monitoring is not a dashboard of pretty charts. It is a disciplined logging habit and a retraining trigger you can defend with evidence.

item.title: A Practical Checklist for Notebook to Production
item.description: A working checklist for taking a model out of a notebook safely, covering data leakage, baselines, monitoring, and the questions reviewers should always ask.

item.title: Image Augmentation: What Actually Generalises
item.description: Most augmentation choices are copied from tutorials rather than justified. Here's how to test which ones actually improve generalisation for your task.

item.title: Object Detection Metrics: mAP Without Hand-Waving
item.description: mAP gets thrown around as a single number, but few people can actually derive it. Here is the arithmetic behind it, worked through by hand.

item.title: Building a Computer Vision Pipeline That Survives Shift
item.description: High test accuracy means little if your test set secretly resembles your training set. Here is how to build vision pipelines that hold up when the world changes.

item.title: Evaluating LLMs Beyond Accuracy
item.description: A single accuracy number hides three separate failure modes in LLMs: unhelpfulness, harm, and hallucination. Each needs its own metric and its own test set.

item.title: LLM Leaderboards: What They Measure and What They Hide
item.description: A high leaderboard rank is not the same as a trustworthy model. Here is what the numbers quietly leave out.

item.title: Feature Stores: Real Problem or Just Ceremony?
item.description: Feature stores promise consistency between training and serving, but the value depends entirely on whether your pipeline actually has that problem.

item.title: Model Registries Explained: Versioning More Than Weights
item.description: A weights file is not a model. Here is what a proper model registry actually needs to track, and why skipping it quietly breaks reproducibility.

item.title: What an MLOps Pipeline Actually Needs Before Kubernetes
item.description: Kubernetes solves a scaling problem you probably don't have yet. Here's what to fix first, from data versioning to leakage-aware evaluation.

item.title: SMOTE and Synthetic Data: When It Backfires
item.description: SMOTE fixes imbalance in theory but often just teaches your model to memorise interpolated noise, especially when it leaks into your test set.

item.title: Overfitting the Validation Set Through Too Many Experiments
item.description: Run enough experiments against one validation set and you stop measuring generalisation, you start measuring luck. Here is why, with numbers.

item.title: Reproducibility: Seeds, Configs, and Runs You Can Rerun
item.description: Most 'irreproducible' ML results fail for boring reasons: unpinned seeds, missing configs, undocumented data splits. Here is how to fix that properly.

item.title: Data Augmentation That Helps vs Augmentation That Leaks
item.description: Augmentation only helps when it happens after splitting. Get the order wrong and your validation score becomes a lie.

item.title: Reading a Confusion Matrix Beyond Accuracy
item.description: Accuracy is a single number that can lie to you. A confusion matrix, read properly, tells you where and why your model actually fails.
